The Collapse of Oversight: When the Watchdogs Feed from the Same Trough

By Dr. Tony Leachon
Independent Health Reform Advocate

The privilege speech of Senator Ping Lacson, “Greed Control,” was a thunderclap—exposing a billion-peso budget mafia operating through ghost flood control projects, padded contracts, and institutional collusion. But what happens when the very agency tasked with auditing corruption is itself entangled in it?

According to government data, a construction company linked to COA Commissioner Mario Lipana’s wife bagged nearly ₱200 million worth of flood control projects from the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) 

The firm, Olympus Mining and Builders Group Philippines Corporation, is led by Marilou Laurio-Lipana, who has confirmed her role as president and general manager. These contracts include major flood control structures in Bulacan—ironically, the same province now under COA’s fraud audit.

This is not just a conflict of interest. It is a collapse of credibility.

How can COA investigate flood control anomalies when one of its own commissioners is directly linked to a beneficiary of those very projects? How can the public trust an audit when the auditor’s household profits from the system it claims to police?

This is the anatomy of complicity.

And yet, Congress—where many of these budget allocations originate—refuses to act. The new Majority Leader has openly admitted that lawmakers cannot probe their own colleagues implicated in Lacson’s exposé. Why? Because too many are involved. Too many have fingerprints on the contracts. Too many have traded their mandate for margins.

This is not gridlock. This is self-preservation.

And what of the Executive Branch?

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has expressed anger. He has inspected ghost projects. He has said, “I’m not disappointed—I’m angry.” But despite overwhelming evidence, he remains gun-shy about firing DPWH Secretary Manuel Bonoan, whose agency sits at the epicenter of the scandal. The President’s hesitation is deafening. It signals that loyalty outweighs accountability, and that rhetoric is enough to pacify a nation drowning in corruption.

So we ask: Where are we going with this?

If COA cannot audit without bias,
If Congress cannot investigate its own,
If the President cannot act with courage,
Then we are not heading toward reform.
We are heading toward collapse.

This is not just a political crisis. It is a moral one.
It is a crisis of conscience, of character, of courage.

We must demand:

• An independent forensic audit of all flood control projects, led by third-party firms with no ties to government
• A congressional ethics tribunal with external oversight to investigate members without bias
• A cabinet purge of officials who obstruct transparency or enable corruption
• A legislative overhaul that criminalizes economic sabotage as a heinous offense, punishable by reclusion perpetua or capital punishment after due process

Because if we do not act now, the rhetoric will rot.
And the Republic will drown—not in floodwaters, but in its own silence.

Let this be the moment we stop pretending.
Let this be the moment we choose justice over loyalty.
Let this be the moment we say: Enough.

#RelentlessForChange

🚨 Traffic Advisory Update – Suchitra X Roads 🚨

Today, DCP Traffic Medchal and ACP Traffic Medchal conducted a field visit at Suchitra X Roads, one of the city's busiest intersections.

🔴 Observation:
Heavy traffic congestion was noted on NH-44, especially towards Qutbullapur and Alwal.

✅ Action Taken:
As per the direction of DCP Traffic Medchal, the U-turn at Suchitra X Roads was temporarily closed to ease traffic flow.

🟢 Current Status:
Traffic movement has now normalized.

📍 Precautionary measures are being implemented to manage pedestrian crossings and ensure smooth vehicular movement.
